passage:
A museum showed a suitcase carried by a family who had moved across the sea. Inside were clothes, letters, a cooking pot, and one toy.
Students were asked what they would pack if they had to leave home quickly.
The room became quiet.
The suitcase made migration feel concrete. It was not only a number in a textbook. It was a decision about what could fit and what had to be left behind.
The guide said every migration story includes both hope and loss.
A suitcase is small, but it can hold a turning point in a family's history.
